description: Design data for brief M4-04 (the sky clock), m4-design §5: instants from 2020 to 2035 at the village with the sun's and the moon's place, the local mean sidereal time, Zurich's UTC offset and the clock's text. Computed once by design (2026-10-17) with a throwaway script outside the repository; nothing in the repository recomputes it.

site.note: The village centre, approximate (m4-design §0). config/sky.json (brief M4-09) holds the area box's centre; design substitutes it here if they differ by more than 1e-3 degrees. The tests pass these values to SkyClock, not config/sky.json's.

sources.sun: pvlib 0.16.1 solarposition.spa_python (NREL SPA), altitude 1610 m, pressure 101325 Pa, temperature 12 C, delta_t computed by pvlib. sun_azimuth_deg: SPA's azimuth, true, clockwise from north. sun_elevation_deg (the expected value): SPA's topocentric true elevation plus NOAA's refraction (the game's model, m4-design §5: 58.1/tan e - 0.07/tan^3 e + 0.000086/tan^5 e above 5 degrees, 1735 - 518.2 e + 103.4 e^2 - 12.79 e^3 + 0.711 e^4 above -0.575, -20.772/tan e below, arcseconds, none above 85). sun_true_elevation_deg and sun_spa_apparent_elevation_deg (SPA's own refraction, applied only above -0.83 degrees) are for reference: below -0.83 SPA adds no refraction where NOAA adds up to 0.47 degrees, more than the band's 0.3 tolerance.
sources.moon: skyfield 1.55 with JPL DE421 (de421.bsp, SHA-256 a20a7139da04cbc462454634918e9a9ca69127044e2cc9d4f9c16e238d2deedc, public domain): topocentric apparent position from the site (WGS84, 1610 m; light time and aberration), no refraction; azimuth true, clockwise from north. moon_illuminated_fraction: as seen from the site.
sources.sidereal: skyfield 1.55 Time.gmst at UT1 = UTC (the game knows only UTC; the true UT1 - UTC is under 0.9 s, 0.004 degrees), times 15, plus the east longitude, in [0, 360).
sources.local: Python 3.13 zoneinfo Europe/Zurich: utcoffset and the text 'D Mon YYYY HH:MM CET|CEST' (minutes truncated, not rounded).

tolerances_deg.note: m4-design §5; the moon's azimuth error is weighted by cos(elevation).

other_sites_note: Other places (the same sources, sea level), so that a site written into the clock or latitude and longitude swapped fail: southern hemisphere, west of Greenwich, far east.
